docs.title: Neon Pricing Plans
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: > Postgres Database, Authentication, and more backend primitives coming soon with three plans: Free, Launch, and Scale. Pay only for what you use on paid plans; no monthly minimum.

docs.title: How billing works
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > How billing works
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Paid plans are pay-as-you-go: usage is metered hourly and billed at the end of the month, with no monthly minimum. Plans apply per **organization**, and one Neon account can belong to multiple orgs on different plans. The Free plan is permanent (not a trial); no credit card…

docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Plans at a glance
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Plans at a glance

docs.title: Plans at a glance
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Plans at a glance
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: All plans include: multi-AZ storage, autoscaling, database branching, read replicas, connection pooling, Postgres extensions (pgvector, PostGIS, TimescaleDB, and more), full management API and CLI, and a Data API for querying over HTTP.

docs.title: Table clarifications
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Table clarifications
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: - **Branches** are capped at 5,000 per project on paid plans (10/25 included). Free is capped at 10 per project. - **Instant restore** is charged only on root branches; child branches don't add to this charge. - **Storage size** has no hard per-branch size limit on paid plans;…

docs.title: How can I try Neon without signing up?
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Common questions > How can I try Neon without signing up?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Use Claimable Neon for an instant project, with no signup and no card. Provision from that page or the API. Claim it to a Neon account before expiration to keep it.

docs.title: What is a project?
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Common questions > What is a project?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Your top-level container: primary database, branches, compute. Like a Git repo, with one project and many branches. Projects belong to **organizations**, where plans and billing apply.

docs.title: How are extra branches billed?
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Common questions > How are extra branches billed?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Branches above your plan's allowance (10 included on Free/Launch, 25 on Scale) are billed at $1.50/branch-month, prorated hourly (~$0.002/hour). Example: 2 extra branches kept for 5 hours each = 10 branch-hours × $0.002 = $0.02.

docs.title: What happens when I hit Free plan limits?
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Common questions > What happens when I hit Free plan limits?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Hitting any Free monthly limit (100 CU-hours, 0.5 GB storage, 5 GB egress) suspends compute until the next billing month. Upgrade to Launch or Scale to resume immediately.

docs.title: How can I control my costs?
docs.heading_path: Neon Pricing Plans > Common questions > How can I control my costs?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: See Cost optimization for the full guide and Reduce network transfer costs for egress.

docs.title: Choosing your connection method
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Your connection method depends on where your code runs. Use the table below for a quick lookup, or read the scenario sections for detailed guidance.

docs.title: Quick reference by environment
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Quick reference by environment
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Quick reference by environment

docs.title: Not using JavaScript or TypeScript?
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Find your scenario > Not using JavaScript or TypeScript?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Use a standard TCP-based Postgres driver with a pooled connection. Connect from a secure backend server using your language's native driver.

docs.title: Running on a long-lived server (JS/TS)?
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Find your scenario > Running on a long-lived server (JS/TS)?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: If you deploy a JavaScript or TypeScript app to Railway, Render, a VPS, Docker, or any self-hosted environment with persistent processes, use a standard TCP driver with connection pooling. Your server can maintain a connection pool across requests, making TCP the fastest and…

docs.title: Deploying to Vercel or Cloudflare with platform pooling?
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Find your scenario > Deploying to Vercel or Cloudflare with platform pooling?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: These platforms provide their own connection pooling, which makes standard TCP the best choice.

docs.title: Deploying to another serverless or edge platform?
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Find your scenario > Deploying to another serverless or edge platform?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: For platforms like Netlify Functions, Deno Deploy, or Cloudflare Workers (without Hyperdrive), use the Neon serverless driver (@neondatabase/serverless). It connects over HTTP or WebSockets instead of TCP, reducing connection setup latency.

docs.title: Building a client-side app without a backend?
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Find your scenario > Building a client-side app without a backend?
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Use the Neon Data API via @neondatabase/neon-js. Browsers cannot open TCP connections to Postgres, so the Data API provides a secure HTTP interface with Row-Level Security support.

docs.title: Pooled vs. direct connections
docs.heading_path: Choosing your connection method > Understanding the options > Pooled vs. direct connections
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: A **pooled connection** routes traffic through PgBouncer, which manages a pool of reusable Postgres connections. Use pooled connections by default. They handle up to 10,000 concurrent client connections and work well for serverless apps and high-concurrency workloads.

docs.heading_path: Pooled
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Pooled postgresql://user:pass@ep-cool-rain-123456-pooler.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require&channel_binding=require

docs.title: Direct
docs.heading_path: Direct
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Direct postgresql://user:pass@ep-cool-rain-123456.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require&channel_binding=require

docs.title: HTTP vs. WebSocket (serverless driver)
docs.heading_path: Direct > HTTP vs. WebSocket (serverless driver)
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: - **HTTP** uses fetch requests. It is faster for single queries (~3 round trips vs. ~8 for TCP) and supports non-interactive transactions. Choose HTTP when your queries are independent, one-shot operations. - **WebSocket** maintains a persistent connection within a request. It…

docs.title: Data API
docs.heading_path: Direct > Data API
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The Data API provides a REST interface to your database over HTTP. It works in browsers, edge runtimes, and anywhere you can make HTTP requests. It validates JWTs from any authentication provider and enforces PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, making it suitable for client-side apps…

docs.title: ORM compatibility
docs.heading_path: Direct > ORM compatibility
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Popular JavaScript and TypeScript ORMs work with Neon across all connection methods. For non-JS/TS ORMs (Django, SQLAlchemy, ActiveRecord, Ecto), use your language's native Postgres driver with a pooled connection.

docs.title: Connection errors
docs.heading_path: Connection errors
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This topic describes how to resolve connection errors you may encounter when using Neon. The errors covered include:

docs.title: The endpoint ID is not specified
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The endpoint ID is not specified
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: With older clients and some native Postgres clients, you may receive the following error when attempting to connect to Neon:

docs.title: A. Pass the endpoint ID as an option
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The endpoint ID is not specified > A. Pass the endpoint ID as an option
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Neon supports a connection option named endpoint, which you can use to identify the compute you are connecting to. Specifically, you can add options=endpoint%3D[endpoint_id] as a parameter to your connection string, as shown in the example below. The %3D is a URL-encoded = sign.…

docs.title: B. Use libpq key=value syntax in the database field
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The endpoint ID is not specified > B. Use libpq key=value syntax in the database field
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: If your application or client is based on libpq but you cannot upgrade the library, such as when the library is compiled inside of a an application, you can take advantage of the fact that libpq permits adding options to the database name. So, in addition to the database name,…

docs.title: C. Set verify-full for golang-based clients
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The endpoint ID is not specified > C. Set verify-full for golang-based clients
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: If your application or service uses golang Postgres clients like pgx and lib/pg, you can set sslmode=verify-full, which causes SNI information to be sent when you connect. Most likely, this behavior is not intended but happens inadvertently due to the golang's TLS library API…

docs.title: D. Specify the endpoint ID in the password field
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The endpoint ID is not specified > D. Specify the endpoint ID in the password field
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Another supported workaround involves specifying the endpoint ID in the password field. So, instead of specifying only your password, you provide a string consisting of the endpoint option and your password, separated by a semicolon (;) or dollar sign character ($), as shown in…

docs.title: Libraries
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The endpoint ID is not specified > Libraries
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Clients on the list of drivers on the PostgreSQL community wiki that use your system's libpq library should work if your libpq version is >= 14.

docs.title: Password authentication failed for user
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Password authentication failed for user
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The following error is often the result of an incorrectly defined connection information, or the driver you are using does not support Server Name Indication (SNI).

docs.title: Couldn't connect to compute node
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Couldn't connect to compute node
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This error arises when the Neon proxy, which accepts and handles connections from clients that use the Postgres protocol, fails to establish a connection with your compute. This issue sometimes occurs due to repeated connection attempts during the compute's restart phase after…

docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Can't reach database server
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: text Error: P1001: Can't reach database server at ep-white-thunder-826300.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech:5432 Please make sure your database server is running at ep-white-thunder-826300.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech:5432.

docs.title: Terminating connection due to administrator command
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Terminating connection due to administrator command
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The terminating connection due to administrator command error is typically encountered when running a query from a connection that has sat idle long enough for the compute to suspend due to inactivity. Neon automatically suspends a compute after 5 minutes of inactivity, by…

docs.title: Unsupported startup parameter
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Unsupported startup parameter
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The error occurs when using a pooled Neon connection string with startup options that are not supported by PgBouncer. PgBouncer allows only startup parameters it can keep track of in startup packets. These include: client_encoding, datestyle, timezone,…

docs.title: You have exceeded the limit of concurrently active endpoints
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > You have exceeded the limit of concurrently active endpoints
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Neon limits concurrently active computes to prevent resource exhaustion. When you exceed the limit, additional computes beyond the limit will remain suspended and you will see this error when attempting to connect to them. You can suspend other active computes and try again.…

docs.title: Remaining connection slots are reserved for roles with the SUPERUSER attribute
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Remaining connection slots are reserved for roles with the SUPERUSER attribute
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This error occurs when the maximum number of simultaneous database connections, defined by the Postgres max_connections setting, is reached.

docs.title: Relation not found
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Relation not found
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This error is often encountered when attempting to set the Postgres search_path session variable using a SET search_path statement over a pooled connection. For more information and workarounds, please see Connection pooling in transaction mode.

docs.title: cannot execute ... in a read-only transaction (SQLSTATE 25006)
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > cannot execute ... in a read-only transaction (SQLSTATE 25006)
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: You attempted a write (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, COPY ... FROM, or DDL such as CREATE, ALTER, DROP, or TRUNCATE) in a transaction that Postgres treats as read-only. The error looks like this:

docs.title: Postgrex: DBConnection ConnectionError ssl send: closed
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Postgrex: DBConnection ConnectionError ssl send: closed
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Postgrex has an :idle_interval connection parameter that defines an interval for pinging connections after a period of inactivity. The default setting is 1000ms. If you rely on Neon's Scale to Zero feature (auto-suspend) to scale your compute to zero when your database is not…

docs.title: query_wait_timeout SSL connection has been closed unexpectedly
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > query_wait_timeout SSL connection has been closed unexpectedly
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The query_wait_timeout setting is a PgBouncer configuration option that determines the maximum time a query can wait in the queue before being executed. Neon's default value for this setting is **120 seconds**. If a query exceeds this timeout while in the queue, it will not be…

docs.title: The request could not be authorized due to an internal error
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > The request could not be authorized due to an internal error
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This error page in the Neon Console is most often the result of attempting to access a Neon project in one browser window after you've have logged in under a different Neon user account from another browser window. The error occurs because the currently logged in Neon user…

docs.title: Terminating connection due to idle-in-transaction timeout
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Terminating connection due to idle-in-transaction timeout
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This error occurs when a session remains idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified timeout period. By default, the idle_in_transaction_session_timeout setting is set to 5min (300,000 milliseconds). This timeout helps prevent idle sessions from holding locks…

docs.heading_path: Connection errors > Error connecting to database: Failed to fetch

docs.snippet: This error appears on the **Tables** page in the Neon Console when the Console's request to your compute doesn't complete:

docs.snippet: Some users encounter DNS resolution failures when connecting to their Neon database. These issues are often reported when using the **Tables** page in the Neon Console. In such cases, users may see an **Unexpected error happened** message like the one below:

docs.title: DNS resolution issues
docs.heading_path: Connection errors > DNS resolution issues
docs.attribution: © Neon — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: - Regional DNS caching or propagation delays - Restrictive or misconfigured DNS resolvers (such as those provided by your ISP) - System-wide web proxy settings that interfere with DNS resolution

docs.title: DNS resolution issues

docs.snippet: Using a VPN routes DNS queries through a different resolver and often bypasses the issue entirely.
